text:
lina: Quick brain dump  can we add a 'what-if replay' in rollouts for automatic fallback policies? i.e. replay the last N minutes of real traffic in a sandbox and show expected fallbacks / cost / latencies.
jorge: Love this. Key ask: preview must respect routing rules (region, model, customer_tier) + any rate limits. otherwise it's meaningless.
tom: We should make the replay deterministic by default (replay same request ids) but offer a randomized mode to stress edge cases.
ashley: From a compliance perspective we need every simulated fallback tied to an auditable record: who ran it, the policy used, and a run-id that appears in the rollout history.
kevin-w: UX idea: inline timeline with hover cards. Each hover shows a short sample trace and a quick reason: "triggered p95 latency" or "model-unavailable". Click to open full trace.
sre-jen: Implementation constraints: we can't replay PII unless teams opt-in. make the replay scrub or hash any sensitive fields. document that clearly in the UI.
lina: Agreed. show a privacy banner: "This replay uses sanitized request payloads" and require a one-time opt-in per team.
eng-bot: Permission check: user lacks role "replay-runner". request link: /access/request?role=replay-runner
jorge: Also add a diff view between baseline and post-fallback metrics: token throughput, median/95 latency, error-rate, estimated token cost.
tom: Can we allow a "sticky session" simulation mode so we can estimate downstream effects of sticky_ttl? e.g. if a route gets sticky fallback for 5 minutes, show how many subsequent requests would still be routed to fallback.
ashley: YES. and if the simulated run toggles a sticky override, capture operator identity in the audit entry and record before/after policy.
kevin-w: For the UI: left = policy editor (text + templates), middle = replay summary + small heatmap, right = audit log / run metadata. big CTA: "Run what-if (sandbox)" with permission gating.
sre-jen: Storage note: keep replay job logs for 90 days, but sampled traces only for 30 days by default. ops can request longer retention via ticket.
lina: Example YAML policy I'd expect to paste into the editor:

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  trigger: "p95_latency_ms > 1000 or error_rate >= 0.05"
  mode: soft-degrade  # soft-degrade | hard-degrade | redirect
  sample_mode: deterministic  # deterministic | stochastic
  sample_rate: 0.2
  sticky_ttl_sec: 180
  attribution: customer_id
```

kevin-w: Nice. UI bits: for sample_rate let people choose slider or exact field. show a tooltip explaining deterministic vs stochastic.
eng-bot: Replay simulated: 12,482 requests sampled, simulated_fallbacks=412 (3.3%), est_median_latency_drop=180ms, est_cost_delta=-6.4% (run: whatif-1767009998).
jorge: Can we export the run as CSV with columns: request_id, route, fallback_reason, trace_link? That will help QA.
tom: Also add a small confidence interval for the cost/latency estimates. people will treat single numbers as gospel otherwise.
sre-jen: I'll add infra checklist: sandbox traffic replayer, scrubbing pipeline, trace-linkback hook, RBAC for replay-runner, retention policy, and audit-store integration.
lina: Thanks. i'll make a quick figma mock and add acceptance criteria: - replay respects routing predicates - scrubbed payloads when opt-in not given - run appears in rollout history with run id - export CSV + trace links - sticky simulation shown.
ashley: Ping me when figma is ready, will run privacy review.
eng-bot: Created ticket RED-PLAT-7310: what-if replay for fallback policy (assignee: platform-ui).
